correctness.rationale: The proof is genuinely infinite and analytic. Under the eventual digit bound \(a_j\le j^2\), four consecutive continued-fraction denominators contain at least two odd denominators, giving two previous odd-multiple distances of order at most \((\log k)^6/k\). Best approximation at the next odd multiple gives a lower bound of order \(1/(k(\log k)^2)\). The source bounds make both forbidden-window functions quadratic in the two small distances, hence of order at most \((\log k)^{12}/k^2\), which is eventually strictly smaller. A finite strict prefix is preserved on a cylinder around the source's explicit admissible rotation number. The exact continued-fraction child-cylinder ratio shows that imposing \(a_j\le j^2\) after a sufficiently deep prefix removes total relative mass less than one, so the surviving set has positive measure; the smooth strictly increasing area map has derivative bounded below on that compact cylinder, preserving positive measure.
risks: The argument imports the source paper's stated bounds for the forbidden-window functions and its explicit admissible base point; those were compared against the primary full text rather than recomputed from the earlier geometric sections.
